title.narrative: Resilient Multifunctional Water Supply systems for Machubo Administrative Post - Marracuene District

description.narrative: The Resilient Multifunctional Water Supply Systems for the Machubo Administrative Post project aims to improve water access, sanitation, and climate resilience in Marracuene District, Mozambique. Implemented by UNDP in collaboration with the Ministry of Public Works, Housing, and Water Resources, this one-year initiative (2024-2025) is funded by the IBSA Fund. condition.narrative: Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

title.narrative: Establishment of a functional system for the management and maintenance of the water system, whether through a community based organization or private service provider.

description.narrative: The indicator "Establishment of a functional system for the management and maintenance of the water system, whether through a community-based organization or private service provider" measures the development and operationalization of a structured, sustainable approach for overseeing the water infrastructure in Machubo. This indicator is qualitative and process-oriented, designed to ensure that a reliable entity is responsible for the upkeep, monitoring, and repairs of the water system to maintain consistent, safe water access. This indicator helps ensure the long-term viability of water access improvements by establishing a reliable entity responsible for maintenance. It supports community resilience, reduces the likelihood of service disruptions, and fosters local empowerment or accountability, depending on whether a CBO or private provider is chosen

title.narrative: Number of inhabitants of Machubo Administrative Post without safe access to water, please provide a description for this indicator

description.narrative: The indicator "Number of inhabitants of Machubo Administrative Post without safe access to water" is a quantitative, outcome-based indicator that measures the population count of people lacking reliable, safe water access in the area. It helps assess the extent of water insecurity in the Machubo Administrative Post and provides a baseline to track progress toward improving access to safe water. This indicator helps stakeholders, including local authorities and NGOs, understand the scale of water access challenges and the effectiveness of initiatives aimed at improving water quality and infrastructure in Machubo. It also allows for evidence-based decision-making, prioritizing interventions for the most affected populations and assessing impacts on health and well-being.

title.narrative: Area of land with improved water management (target: 700 ha)

description.narrative: The indicator measures the extent (in hectares) of land that has been enhanced through water management practices aimed at promoting sustainable use, increasing water availability, and improving soil and crop productivity. With a target of 700 hectares, this indicator reflects progress in expanding areas where water management improvements have been implemented to benefit agricultural or natural landscapes.

title.narrative: Number of evidence-based good practices documented based on the achievements of the South Africa-UN Fund projects

description.narrative:
The indicator measures the extent to which successful strategies and approaches used in these projects are captured, evaluated, and recorded for future reference. This documentation is crucial for sharing replicable solutions across similar development contexts, enabling learning and scaling of effective practices.
Good practices are strategies or interventions from South Africa-UN Fund projects that have demonstrated positive outcomes and can be adapted by other initiatives. They must be supported by clear evidence, such as improved community health, increased agricultural productivity, or enhanced water resource management.

title.narrative: Number of South-South cooperation knowledge exchanges supported/facilitated by the South Africa-UN Fund project

description.narrative: The indicator measures the number of formal knowledge-sharing activities between developing countries, facilitated by the South Africa-UN Fund. This indicator reflects the Fund’s role in promoting collaboration and learning among countries in the Global South, enabling them to share expertise, innovative solutions, and experiences to address similar development challenges.

title.narrative: Number of examples of good practices in South-South cooperation transferred to developing countries with support by the South Africa-UN Fund project

description.narrative: The indicator measures the successful sharing of innovative, effective practices from one developing country to another, facilitated by the South Africa-UN Fund. South-South cooperation emphasizes the exchange of resources, knowledge, and skills among developing countries, with the goal of empowering them through mutual support and shared solutions.

title.narrative: Number of families benefited through improved water management (target: 1,100)

description.narrative: The indicator tracks the number of households that have gained access to more reliable, efficient, and sustainable water resources through enhanced water management practices. This indicator, with a target of 1,100 families, serves as a quantitative measure of the social impact and reach of water management initiatives.

title.narrative: Number of Farmers (Male/Female) Trained in the Use of Agricultural Water Management Practices

description.narrative: This indicator counts the number of farmers who receive training in improved agricultural water management practices. The goal is to equip male and female farmers with skills to optimize water use in agriculture, increase productivity, and boost income from farming

title.narrative: Rehabilitation of School Toilets in 1 School

description.narrative: This indicator measures the completion of rehabilitation work on the toilets of the largest secondary school in the district. The focus is on ensuring that the toilets are fully functional, hygienic, and adequately equipped for daily use by students and staff. Rehabilitation activities may include repairing or installing plumbing, ensuring proper waste disposal, upgrading handwashing facilities, and enhancing ventilation.

title.narrative: Number of Beneficiary Community Members Trained in Sustainable Use of Multifunctional Water Systems

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of individuals in the community who have received training on the sustainable use and upkeep of the multifunctional water systems. This training promotes awareness and skills needed to use these systems effectively and ensure their longevity.

title.narrative: Number of households using the multifunctional standpipes in Machubo Administrative Post.

description.narrative: This indicator measures the uptake and utilization of shared standpipe water systems by households within the designated area. This indicator is a quantitative, utilization-based measure, designed to assess the reach and effectiveness of the standpipe infrastructure in providing safe and accessible water to residents.

title.narrative: Completion of a design study laying out the most effective way of ensuring safe water access to all inhabitants and key public infrastructure of Machubo Administrative Post.

description.narrative: This indicator refers to a measurable outcome that assesses whether a comprehensive, evidence-based design plan has been developed. This study should include an actionable strategy for providing safe, sustainable, and equitable water access to both residential areas and crucial facilities like healthcare centers, schools, and government offices within Machubo.

title.narrative: Creation of an effective system of maintenance of water and drainage infrastructure, with or without the contracting of a private service provider

description.narrative: This indicator tracks the establishment of a functional, sustainable system to manage and maintain the water and drainage infrastructure in beneficiary communities. This system could be managed by a community-based organization or contracted to a private provider through a transparent selection process.

title.narrative: Number of Children (Male/Female) Using the Rehabilitated Toilet Facilities

description.narrative: This indicator tracks the number of students (disaggregated by gender) who regularly use the rehabilitated toilet facilities. It provides insight into the accessibility, usability, and acceptance of the new facilities by students, as well as the potential impact on school attendance and hygiene practices.

title.narrative: Increase in agricultural production and farmer (male / female) income from the improved water management (target: 50% increase over average of recent years).

description.narrative: The indicator measures the impact of water management interventions on agricultural productivity and the associated economic benefits for farmers, with a target of a 50% increase over the average of recent years. This indicator is a quantitative, outcome-based measure, aimed at assessing both crop yield improvements and income gains for male and female farmers resulting from enhanced water management practices.
